description: Every engine item that SinkBroom's lit preview mirrors, or deliberately does not copy, with the engine commit it was read at. Checked before each landing by TOOLS/lit_mirror_check.py (LP-M).

rules.lines: first and last line, 1-based and inclusive, in the file at engineCommit
rules.anchor: the function, member or symbol that holds the range, for finding it again once the engine's line numbers move
rules.sha256: of the range's text at engineCommit: each line without its line ending, followed by \n
rules.sinkbroom: the SinkBroom file and symbol that mirror the range or say why not
rules.testOnly: true for an engine copy (and its shim) linked by TbLitLibTest alone, never by the product: the LP1c fix round's fast DXT encoders for the image goldens (S3.2; D24 bars CPU BC encoding from the product only)

kinds.dispatcher: the vulkan.hpp dynamic dispatcher's storage and initialisation
kinds.instance: a property of the Vulkan instance
kinds.device-extension: a device extension and the code that enables it
kinds.feature-chain: device features that are checked and enabled
kinds.function: engine code mirrored with the stated differences
kinds.constant: an engine value used as is
kinds.not-copied: engine code deliberately not mirrored, with the reason
kinds.copied-file: an engine file copied whole and byte for byte into lib/TbLitLib/idtech/engine; gitBlob is its git blob id at engineCommit
kinds.copied-range: engine line ranges copied verbatim into a partial file under lib/TbLitLib/idtech/engine, each preceded by one marker line
kinds.build: how TbLitIdLib is compiled: the engine's C++ standard and the compile definitions the copied files branch on
kinds.table: an engine table mirrored row for row
kinds.shim-virtual: a virtual of a copied or engine class that the shim defines, so the vtables link
kinds.fatal-site: a never-returning engine call (Error, FatalError) in the copied or mirrored code, which the shim turns into log-and-return, with what the code does after it returns
kinds.static: a static or global of the copied code (or the shim's bindings), its kind and why it needs no reset
kinds.temporary: a stand-in that a later package replaces
kinds.guard: a check outside the copied code that keeps a latent engine fault from being reached
kinds.difference: a deliberate difference from the engine's behaviour, with its reason
kinds.known-defect: an engine defect the copy keeps verbatim, with its effect
kinds.pure-function: copied engine code that the facade lets any thread run, because it touches no state
kinds.pool-safe: copied engine code, or a shim function around it, that may run on the session's CPU pool under C24's five conditions: (1) its common and idLib::common calls go to the permanent sink of D63; (2) each FatalError site in it is listed with the pre-validation that keeps it unreachable; (3) SIMDProcessor is the scalar stand-in; (4) it allocates with the tagged new and Mem_Alloc16 on the global allocator; (5) its statics are constant-initialised, or dynamically initialised at program load from literals alone, without allocating, opening, loading or starting anything and without depending on another file's statics beyond zero (R1.6: the dynamic initialisers allowed are listed in M-ID-STATIC-39 and checked by TOOLS/lit-preview/check_static_init.py), and read-only (the statics inventory)

The engine loads the library itself; SinkBroom takes vkGetInstanceProcAddr from Qt (C9), a host outside SinkBroom from lit::VulkanInstance (LPF.2, M-INST-02).

engine.anchor: DeviceManager_VK::createInstance, API 1.2 and the portability flag

entries.note: LPF.2 (D107, P5.11, C9, P5.29): a host's instance outside SinkBroom (the Mixar side's, and the tests'); the engine's DeviceManager_VK makes its own with a static vk::DynamicLoader. Both ask for Vulkan 1.2 and the platform's surface extensions (the engine: VK_KHR_surface and VK_KHR_win32_surface, or SDL's list; the host: win32, or xcb, xlib and wayland as the loader offers them, or VK_EXT_metal_surface, only when it presents) and on macOS VK_KHR_portability_enumeration with VK_INSTANCE_CREATE_ENUMERATE_PORTABILITY_BIT_KHR. Differences: the loader is loaded by create (LoadLibraryW, dlopen) and unloaded at destroy, never at static initialisation (C9); vkEnumerateInstanceVersion is asked first and a loader below 1.2 is an error with the reason (the engine's FatalError on a failed createInstance becomes a Result); the validation layer is enabled only when listed (R-B16) and reports through VK_EXT_debug_utils to the host's sink (the engine: VK_EXT_debug_report and installDebugCallback, M-NC-06), whose duplicate_message_limit the host may raise through VK_EXT_layer_settings; the engine's VK_LAYER_MESSAGE_ID_FILTER (OutputNotConsumed and MipMapGen's by-design messages) is not set: a host sees M-PIPE-DEFECT-01's warnings; MoltenVK's layer settings are not passed. No SinkBroom path constructs it: the editor's instance is QVulkanInstance (M-INST-01), and the panel's C9 test is unchanged. Built and run on Windows only; the Linux and macOS paths are the user's checklist (LPF-CHECKLIST)
Required: VK_KHR_swapchain (only when presenting; the headless test path does not need it) and VK_KHR_maintenance1.

Optional VK_KHR_synchronization2 with VkPhysicalDeviceSynchronization2FeaturesKHR::synchronization2 chained after the 1.2 features. It switches NVRHI's barriers to vkCmdPipelineBarrier2 (nvrhi vulkan-state-tracking.cpp:345), so the preview takes the game's barrier path. Dropped when the extension is listed but the feature is not.
Optional VK_EXT_memory_budget, the VRAM budget's source (S9, LP2).

VkPhysicalDeviceFeatures: shaderImageGatherExtended, samplerAnisotropy, textureCompressionBC, imageCubeArray, dualSrcBlend on; shaderStorageImageReadWithoutFormat, tessellationShader, geometryShader, fillModeNonSolid as supported. The five forced features are checked at device choice (the engine checks only samplerAnisotropy and textureCompressionBC there; the others would fail vkCreateDevice).

VkPhysicalDeviceVulkan12Features in DeviceCreateInfo::pNext: descriptorIndexing, runtimeDescriptorArray, descriptorBindingPartiallyBound, descriptorBindingVariableDescriptorCount, timelineSemaphore (NVRHI's queue tracking), shaderSampledImageArrayNonUniformIndexing; each is checked at device choice.

pickPhysicalDevice: per device the required extensions, features, B8G8R8A8_UNORM surface format, FIFO and present support; the first discrete GPU, else the first other device, in enumeration order. Added: Vulkan 1.2 or newer (S12), and the error text lists every device with its problems instead of FatalError. Changed: the surface's formats and present modes are asked only of a device with a family that presents to the surface, as the specification requires, and a device whose queries throw is skipped with a log line instead of ending the choice (review L3.3).

findQueueFamilies and the queue create infos. The engine takes the first graphics family and the first present family separately and may create two queues; the preview requires one family that does both, creates one queue and keeps the swapchain images exclusive.
Timer queries only when timestampPeriod > 0 and the family's timestampValidBits > 0; otherwise the frame log's GPU column stays empty.

nvrhi::vulkan::DeviceDesc with the enabled instance and device extensions, graphics queue only; nvrhi::validation::createValidationLayer in Debug with SessionOptions::validation (the engine: r_useValidationLayers). errorCB is the session's own callback, which counts errors and sets the lost flag (R5.19), instead of DefaultMessageCallback, which turns errors into FatalError.
Swapchain format RGBA8_UNORM swapped to B8G8R8A8_UNORM. The engine always pairs it with SRGB_NONLINEAR; the preview takes the colour space of the surface's matching format entry.
Swapchain image count NUM_FRAME_DATA = 3, clamped to the surface's minImageCount and maxImageCount (0 = no limit).

engine.anchor: DeviceManager_VK::createSwapChain, the whole function Swapchain.cpp:30 cites (its parts in M-SWAP-01, M-SWAP-03, M-SWAP-04, M-NC-01 and M-NC-02)

entries.note: VkSwapchainCreateInfoKHR: usage ColorAttachment | TransferDst | Sampled, one array layer, identity pre-transform, opaque composite alpha, clipped, no old swapchain. The preview falls back to the current transform and the first supported alpha mode when identity or opaque is not offered, and always uses exclusive sharing (one family).
Swapchain image wrappers: createHandleForNativeTexture(VK_Image) with initialState Present, keepInitialState, isRenderTarget.

The engine clamps its back-buffer size into the surface's range. The preview uses currentExtent, takes the passed window size only when currentExtent is 0xFFFFFFFF, and makes no swapchain for 0×0 (§3.1).

The engine's r_swapInterval / r_vkPreferFastSync choice among MAILBOX, IMMEDIATE, FIFO_RELAXED and FIFO. The preview uses MAILBOX if offered, else FIFO, and FIFO when forced (D48, R5.4); IMMEDIATE only if LP0 measures FIFO's present blocking beyond a bound.

The engine acquires with an infinite timeout and asserts on the result, and cycles one semaphore per image for both acquire and present. The preview acquires with a 50 ms timeout (D48) through the vk::Result overloads, skips on TIMEOUT or NOT_READY, posts SwapchainOutOfDate on OUT_OF_DATE or SUBOPTIMAL, and keeps acquire semaphores per frame in flight and present semaphores per image, all owned by the swapchain generation.

The engine's single frame event query, waited per NUM_FRAME_DATA. The preview keeps a ring of kFramesInFlight event queries and waits on frame N - 2's before recording frame N (D35). The wait polls the event query and ends on a stop or a park, where NVRHI's waitEventQuery would wait without a bound (review L2.1).

Optional device extensions and features the preview does not need: VK_EXT_debug_marker (debug utils replaces it), VK_EXT_descriptor_indexing (its features are core 1.2 and enabled through VkPhysicalDeviceVulkan12Features), VK_KHR_buffer_device_address and bufferDeviceAddress (ray tracing only; the engine notes it 'only makes problems'), VK_NV_mesh_shader, VK_KHR_fragment_shading_rate and its features, VK_KHR_format_feature_flags2, VK_GOOGLE_display_timing and hostQueryReset (Optick), the ray-tracing extensions, the macOS portability subset.

Instance extensions: VK_KHR_get_physical_device_properties2 (core since 1.1; the instance is 1.2), VK_EXT_sampler_filter_minmax (listed by the engine as an instance extension, but it is a device extension and its feature is never enabled), VK_EXT_debug_report and its callback (replaced by VK_EXT_debug_utils, which Qt adds for its debug output redirect when the session validates; lit::VulkanInstance, a host's and the tests' instance, asks for it itself, M-INST-02). Qt adds the surface extensions.
The VK_LAYER_MESSAGE_ID_FILTER environment variable: a process-wide setting; LP0 creates no pipelines, whose warnings it filters. Revisit when pipelines arrive (LP2).
The D24S8 format probe, the VMA allocator, the push-constant size and Optick's GPU init: not used by LP0. The push-constant size and the depth format come with the passes (LP2, C2).
Compute and transfer queues: the preview submits everything, uploads included, on the graphics queue (S35).

The engine's destruction order (waitIdle, semaphores, swapchain, device handle, VkDevice, surface, instance) never collects NVRHI garbage. The preview follows §3.1's teardown steps instead: release handles, waitForIdle, runGarbageCollection (skipped when lost), wrappers, vkDestroySwapchainKHR, semaphores, the NVRHI device with its last Release() count, then the VkDevice; the surface and the instance belong to Qt.

linkOptions.name: /OPT:REF
linkOptions.when: MSVC Release links of every target that links TbLitLib, only with TB_ENABLE_LIT_PREVIEW (an INTERFACE option of the static TbLitLib: TbLitLibTest, and through TbUiLib the final links of TrenchBroom.exe, DumpShortcuts and TbUiLibTest)
linkOptions.why: G12: TrenchBroom.exe's Release link passes /DEBUG (app/TrenchBroom/CMakeLists.txt), whose default is /OPT:NOREF, so the copied Str.cpp's six thread_local buffers (192 KB, M-ID-STATIC-30..35) stayed in its static TLS although nothing calls their functions. The other links have no /DEBUG and drop them already. It removes every library's unreferenced code from TrenchBroom.exe, not only Str.cpp's: the user decides whether that stays (14-LP1A-FIXES-2.md D); if not, the options go and the 192 KB are recorded as accepted

linkOptions.name: /OPT:NOICF
linkOptions.when: MSVC Release links of every target that links TbLitLib, only with TB_ENABLE_LIT_PREVIEW (an INTERFACE option of the static TbLitLib: TbLitLibTest, and through TbUiLib the final links of TrenchBroom.exe, DumpShortcuts and TbUiLibTest)
linkOptions.why: W.8 (round 2): an explicit /OPT:REF also folds identical functions (/OPT:ICF) unless /OPT:NOICF is given. Folded functions share one address, so a cpptrace stack trace from the stripped PDB can name the folded twin, and pointer-to-member comparisons of identical bodies compare equal (Qt's PMF-based disconnect). NOICF keeps every function apart; in the links without /DEBUG it turns off the folding they had by default

entries.tls: the six thread_local buffers of the copied Str.cpp (M-ID-STATIC-30..35, three 4 x MAX_PRINT_MSG buffers, 192 KB) are static TLS in every thread of a binary that keeps them; the copy never calls their functions. dumpbin /tls, raw data (G12, 2026-10-21): TrenchBroom.exe Release before LP1a 0x273C, a Release link of the LP1a.2 state 0x3276C (+0x30030: kept, because TrenchBroom's Release link passes /DEBUG, which turns /OPT:REF off), TbUiLibTest Release 0x2891 (linked without /DEBUG, so /OPT:REF drops them), TbLitLibTest Debug 0x39DA4, TrenchBroom.exe Debug 0x3CAE3. Fix (linkOptions): /OPT:REF /OPT:NOICF on every MSVC Release link that uses TbLitLib. Measured at round 2 (W.8): TrenchBroom.exe Release 0x273C and 21,978,112 bytes (with /OPT:REF alone, folding: 0x273C and 19,984,384 bytes; without either, 41.5 MB), TbUiLibTest Release 0x2891, TrenchBroom.exe Debug 0x3CAE3. Debug keeps the buffers: accepted LP1c.2: stb_image's failure reason and load flags are plain statics, not thread-local (STBI_NO_THREAD_LOCALS, M-IMG-BUILD-01), so they add nothing to the TLS block: Release TrenchBroom.exe 0x273C again (LP1c fix S1.4)

ListFiles takes the names from the DeclSource (GetFileList's part, which lit/GameFileSource.h mirrors, M-FS-01), adds each once case-insensitively and sorts with idSort_PathStr. ReadFile returns a Mem_Alloc'ed, NUL-terminated buffer of length + 1, -1 and FILE_NOT_FOUND_TIMESTAMP for an unreadable file. Not in the engine (R5.20): once the registry's cancel flag is set, every later ReadFile returns an empty file without asking the source, so the copied RegisterDeclFolder loop ends after the file it was reading and nothing is reported. The exception boundary (C17, G3): a source call that throws is reported as a warning, and the copy sees an unreadable file or an empty folder. ReadFile also refuses, with a warning, a file of 2 GB or more (the engine's lengths are ints) and one M-ID-GUARD-06 refuses. A5 (LP1c.1): ReadFile with no buffer (the loaders' and GetTimestamp's time-only calls) asks the source's probe, which reads no file body (M-FS-08), and returns the probe's length, or -1 and FILE_NOT_FOUND_TIMESTAMP for no file. D63: common and idLib::common point to one idCommon, tbLitCommonSink, from the start of the process and are never rebound; its Printf, Warning, Error and FatalError (and idLib's message functions, AssertFailed and the file system's warnings) format the message on the calling thread and push it, tagged with that thread, into one queue under a mutex. Constant-initialised: the queue's constructor is constexpr (std::mutex, two null node pointers and a count), and it allocates a node only when a message is pushed (C9, S27); nodes still queued at exit are not freed. Pushing never throws (C17): a message that cannot be kept (no room, no memory) is counted for the thread that lost it, in a fixed table of 64 slots claimed by the thread id's hash (B0.5, R2.5, R2.6: never another thread's, never another session's; a discard frees the slot; V.7: the thread's own slot is looked for in all 64 before a free one is claimed, so that no thread holds two); that thread's next drain ends with a Warning that says how many were dropped and an Error that says how many of them were errors, which the registry adds to its own error count and which fails a CPU job. B0.6: TB_LIT_CONSTINIT has the compiler check the constant initialisation where it can (constinit, Clang's require_constant_initialization, GCC's __constinit; MSVC compiles the shim as C++17 and has none); the queue's mutex is destroyed at exit, after every thread that pushes has been joined. The registry drains its own thread's messages (Registry::messages, takeMessages, errorCount, beginCapture, endCapture) and drops those its thread pushed before it was made and while it is destroyed, as no registry received them before; any other thread's are drained by that thread's owner with drainEngineMessagesForThread (the CPU pool's, LP1b.2). Any thread; since LP1b.2 (D66, B0.1) each CpuPool job drops its thread's leftover messages before it and drains them into its CpuJobResult after it, the queue holds at most 4096 messages (beyond: dropped, counted for the thread, reported by its next drain), and a pool thread discards its messages when it ends

entries.note: ParseStage warns at the 257th stage but does not return, and writes past pd->parseStages[256] on the parse thread's stack (A2.4; the engine at the pinned commit has the same defect). After numStages++ it also writes a coverage stage at parseStages[numStages] with no limit check when the stage is diffuse and alpha-tested (engine Material.cpp:2298-2302, the copy's 2299-2303), so one call can write two slots. Before anything can parse it, every material decl whose text can make more than 256 slots is made the default material, with the engine's warning, and its lookup fails with that reason. The bound comes from the copied idLexer's tokens with DECL_LEXER_FLAGS (forEachDeclToken, the tokens idMaterial::Parse reads): after the first "{" (SkipUntilString), every token equal to "{" counts 1 and every stage shortcut keyword 2, whatever its type and wherever it stands. ParseMaterial calls ParseStage only for such a token, once per token. A stage is diffuse only through ParseBlend's diffusemap or basecolormap: in a "{" block that is a token of the material's text, counted 2, which pays for the block's coverage slot; a shortcut's stage is parsed from synthesised text holding its image name without the quotes (AppendToken), so diffusemap "_white alphaTest 0.5" makes two slots that its second count pays for. AddImplicitStages adds at most one stage, below the limit, without an alpha test. So the bound is never below the slots the engine writes; it is above them where such a token is an argument, a block's own keyword or text after a parse error (M-ID-DIFF-03). W.1 (round 2) replaced a character scan of brace depth that crafted text got past ('diffusemap {', 'qer_editorimage {', the lexer's '/*/' comment, '.5diffusemap'); X.1 (round 3) counts shortcuts twice for the coverage stage. LPF.0b (C42): re-applied to a text handed in for a re-parse (MaterialDecls::feedTextGuards, after the token guard, as at construction), which refuses it with the engine's reason and leaves the decl as it was; a kept file text restore sets back is checked again, and one it refuses is made the default as at construction

a decl file holding a token of MAX_STRING_CHARS or more characters with no '.' among the first MAX_STRING_CHARS is refused with a warning and read as unreadable (the copied LoadAndParse then reports 'couldn't load'), because any token can reach MakeNameCanonical and overflow its buffer. The tokens are the copied idLexer's with DECL_LEXER_FLAGS over the whole file (forEachDeclToken, which silences only the lexer's printing with LEXFL_NOERRORS and LEXFL_NOWARNINGS and goes on after a token it cannot read wherever the lexer moved forward; the decl parsers go on there too, while LoadAndParse stops at a failed top-level read, so the scan reads a superset of the tokens the engine reads), so strings joined across a backslash, '...' literals with spaces, a name after a number and the lexer's comment rules are read exactly as the engine reads them; tokens inside comments are not tokens. A dot ends the canonical name first, so the retail PDAs' long texts are read (newpdas/enpro_hammer.pda: a 1075-character string whose first dot is its fifth character). A known difference: the engine reads such a file and overruns. W.1 (round 2) replaced a character scan of names and quoted strings that crafted text got past. LP1c.2 (LP1c.1's follow-up 3): the scan runs on decl reads only; the copied image loaders' reads (between beginImageReads and endImageReads) go through readGameFile and the loader pre-validation instead (M-IMG-GUARD-01). a folder's files with an extension over every source, in GetFileList's order: the resource files (searchPaths and containers from the last), each in its table's order, then the .pk4 files the same way, then the loose files; a container entry only when it lies directly in the folder (allowSubdirsForResourcePaks is false), with GetFileList's own tests, case-insensitively, its trailing slashes stripped. the containers of <game path>/base in registration order: Sys_ListFiles( base, ".resources" ) sorted with idSort_PathStr, then Sys_ListFiles( base/maps, ".resources" ) sorted, each with "maps/" in front; then Sys_ListFiles( base, ".pk4" ) sorted. A .pk4 holding binary.conf is refused without a message, as Init refuses it. A container whose Init fails is skipped with the engine's warning. On Windows the first listing recurses and lists base/maps' containers too; the engine then registers them twice, and SinkBroom keeps each once at its later place, which finds the same file for every name (M-FS-DIFF-04). With fs_resourceLoadPriority 0, a read searches each kind from the last registered: base/maps' .resources (z to a), then base's (z to a); .pk4 files z to a. LP6.3 (A52, C67 (a)): the engine reads every container's table again at each start (AddGameDirectory, FileSystem.cpp:3174); the preview keeps the tables under their key (the base folder made absolute, the listing in this order, each container's name, size and stamp; lit/GameContainerIndex.h) across Stop and in a file under the user-data folder, reuses them while the key stands and scans when it moved, the search unchanged

fs_resourceLoadPriority 0 (its default): the loose file first, then the .pk4 files, then the resource files, each kind searched from its last registered container (M-FS-02). A leading slash is dropped; a path holding .. or ::, or an empty one, finds nothing; a container lookup refuses a path with a colon (an OS path), and compares the path with backslashes made slashes, case-insensitively. A container's file has time 0 (the engine wraps it in an idFile_Memory); a loose file's time is its modification time in whole Unix seconds, as Sys_FileTimeStamp gives it (A4, LP1c.1; M-FS-08). LP1c.1: the search serves every game file the preview reads (C8, C10): readFile for decl text, readGameFile for the image caches and bakes, which never asks for another build

the header (big-endian magic 0xD000000D, table offset, table length), the table (big-endian count; per entry a little-endian name length, the name, big-endian offset and length; a negative name length reads no name), names with backslashes made slashes and ASCII lowercased (CharIsUpper also accepts 0xC0-0xDF, but char is signed in the engine's builds), the later of two entries with one name first (Add puts the newer at the head of its chain), an entry's bytes at offset. Not in the engine: every offset and length is checked against the file before it is read (M-FS-DIFF-03)

a .pk4's entries as Init stores them, backslashes made slashes and lowercased, read through TrenchBroom's ZipFileSystem (D55), which skips directory entries (GetFileList skips them too) and keeps the later of two entries whose names differ only in case (ImageFileSystemBase::addFile), as the engine's hash finds it; an entry is read with ZipFileSystem::openFile

on Windows the folder and every folder below it, names relative to the folder with forward slashes, a file's long name matched by PathMatchSpecW against *<extension> (a case-insensitive suffix); elsewhere the folder alone, fnmatch( *<extension>, name, 0 ) (case-sensitive) and no directory. So on Windows a loose decl file in a subfolder of materials is read, as the engine reads it. Not in the engine: a folder that cannot be read lists nothing and the others are still listed (each folder has its own iterator); a name that is not valid Unicode is skipped, with a warning when it is a folder or matches the extension (G3); the listing stops within one directory entry once the cancel flag is set (G4)

a loose file at <game path>/base/<path>; on POSIX, when the path does not open, the file in the same folder whose path equals it case-insensitively. Opened with share-read, share-write and share-delete on Windows, where the engine shares read only (M-FS-DIFF-02)

C1: one search path, <game path>/base, from Map::gamePath(). No mod, fs_game, fs_game_base or fs_savepath is searched: the engine adds fs_savepath after fs_basepath and each mod after base, and searches the newest first

R4-3.26, A2.15: loose and .resources files are opened per read batch with share-read, share-write and share-delete, so the user can save or replace them while the preview runs; every container closes at the end of the batch. A .pk4 is opened by TbFsLib's createCFile (_wfopen, which shares read and write but not delete) for its batch only: TbFsLib is not changed (C12)

a container that the engine would quit on (a wrong magic, FatalError) or read out of bounds (a header, table or entry that does not fit in the file) is refused, or the entry dropped, with a warning; a container that changed after its table was read is not read from. A name is cut at its first NUL, as the engine's C-string lookups see it
a container listed twice (base/maps on Windows) is registered once, at its later place; the engine opens it twice, and its earlier copy never finds a file that the later one does not find first

a reload builds a new registry from a new source (the containers are scanned again; LP6.3, A52: a source from the lit panel's container index checks the containers' key and scans them only when it moved) instead of the engine's per-file Reload, and re-parses the names the consumers asked for before it publishes; only loose decl folders are polled (R4-3.26). G5, G6 (A2.3, A3.5, A3.6): the loose decl files' times, unreadable ones included, are stamped before and after each build; a build whose stamps differ, or whose source read a loose file that kept changing (stat before and after each read, three attempts), asks for one more build, and a change found by a poll does too, at most once per autoReloadInterval (5 s). A file that lists but cannot be read is reported once (the copied 'couldn't load') and builds nothing until its time changes; case-differing loose duplicates on POSIX stamp alike before and after, so they never loop

A3.11: AddUnique hashes case-sensitively, so a loose Foo.mtr and a container's foo.mtr are both listed; RegisterDeclFolder folds them with Icmp but runs LoadAndParse twice, which is idempotent and reports its warnings twice. SinkBroom folds case-insensitively and keeps the first spelling (the container's lowercase one), so a material's source file can differ in case. entries.note: LP1c.1 (C8, D23, A3): the cache file through the C8 search (OpenFileRead: loose, then .pk4, then .resources), read and time-tested as LoadFromGeneratedFile; when that fails and resource files are in use, the BFHACK name the same way; a loaded cache is used when its colour format, format (RGBA8 for RGB565, R11G11B10F for BC6H) and texture type equal DeriveOpts'. Where the engine would binarize, the preview reports Missing (no file) or Stale (a file it would not use, with the engine's binarize reason) for LP1c.2's fallback; it never writes. The editor image is never asked (C8)

LP1c.1: every count and size is checked before it is used: a header shorter than 36 bytes (the engine reads it as it is), a negative or impossible level count, a negative data size, an odd RGB565 level (the engine's in-place expansion reads misaligned pairs) or a level cut short fails the read, where the engine reads garbage or past the end; the preview then reports the cache Stale. A block-compressed level keeps its stored bytes: the engine pads its own allocation to NVRHI's row pitch times the rows, which LP2 does at upload LP1c fix (S3.5): the header's sides must be 1 to 16384 and its level count 1 to the levels its larger side halves into; each level record must be the one the engine's binarizer writes at its place (record k of a 2D image is level k, side 0; of a cube level k / 6, side k % 6: level-major), of that level's size (max(1, side >> level); a block format's cube level below 4 padded to 4) and with at least the bytes its format needs for that size (whole 4 x 4 blocks for DXT1, DXT5, BC6H, BC7, ETC1; the engine asserts dataSize >= w * h * bpp / 8); else the cache is Stale with the reason and never Ready, so LP2 never uploads a shape its header does not state

LP1c.1: the preview mirrors the engine as SinkBroom's users build it: STANDALONE off (TD_LIGHT is RGB565; a STANDALONE build stores RGBA8, which the match accepts for RGB565 anyway) and com_productionMode 0 (the time call runs and the staleness test applies; production mode trusts any cache)

entries.note: LP1c.1: an image's slot is read once per session, when it is first asked for, and kept across material reloads (it does not depend on the decls); the engine reads it at every image load. LP1c.2 (LP1c.1's follow-up 5): the poll re-reads a slot when a loose file it was read from or its time call found changes (its time, size or change stamp; M-IMG-DIFF-06), so a saved source or a new cache is seen; a file in a container, a file that appears where none was, or a reload's new containers are seen after a restart of the session LP1c fix (S2.5, S3.4): the time call's probes that missed are recorded too (the .tga default, the png/tga/jpg/exr/hdr loop, the _rmao sibling; not the cache names), so a texture written after its material is seen at the next poll, and the slot read again; a reload drops every slot (M-IMG-DIFF-09). New containers, and caches the engine writes into one, are seen through a reload (materialCollectionsDidChange) or a new session LP1c fix round 2 (X.3, X.5): a slot keeps every file it was read from or looked for, container entries and the cache names a read missed included, and the poll compares them by kind, container and time (and size and change stamp for a loose file): a loose file over a container entry, or a cache the engine writes later as a loose file, is seen at the next poll, a new container's at the next reload. The C21 sizes keep every file alike LP1c fix round 3 (Y.2): a container entry's probe carries the container file's own change stamp and size from when its table was read (not compared by ==), so a container rebuilt in place reads as changed after a reload and its slots are dropped

entries.note: LP7.0 (C51, C52, C53, D126, P7.19, P7.20): the engine loads a model synchronously on the calling thread (GetModel) and keeps it in its model list by canonical name; the preview's model table is the material service's, published with the materials (C20), so a record has states of its own: Pending (requested, read or finishing: its entities draw nothing and keep the frame unconverged, D124), Ready, Missing (no file: the default cube, flagged) and Default (an unknown type, a validator or loader failure, a modelDef name on an idEntity spawnclass: the cube, flagged). A record carries per surface the material, EngineDrawVert vertices, 16-bit indexes, generateNormals, tangentsCalculated and bounds; the model bounds, the three has-surfaces flags, the source kind (binary, source, default), the source time (A4, the file source's), the binary's stored time (LoadBinaryModel's test is LP7.1a's), a .bglb's model_state and animation count (P7.19), a version and the notice's reason. MaterialTable::models is kept across reloads with modelChanges and changedModels, as the images' slots are (a model does not depend on the decls; LP7.1a's source path re-finishes records whose materials change, P7.22); MaterialTable::skins is per registry, as the entityDefs. LP7.0 has no loader and no request path: the maps are empty, so every model name finds no record. The skins are not reachable from the parse thread through the facade today: the shim registers DECL_SKIN with the copied idDeclSkin (DeclManagerShim.cpp Init, Init2: the skins folder) and the registry parses a skin when FindSkin asks, but MaterialDecls has no skin call and idDeclSkin's mappings are private (RemapShaderBySkin is its only lookup), so the map stays empty until LP7.2 adds a facade call. The frame log carries LP7's eleven counts (model_entities, model_instances, model_draws, models_pending, models_skinned, dress_surfaces, dress_unmatched, adopted_islands, adopted_tris, unmatched_islands, curved_islands) after proc_bytes at the end of the header, 0 in every frame row until LP7.2-LP7.4 fill them, empty in start and stop rows: 69 fields LP7.1a: the table is filled (MaterialService::requestModel, M-MODEL-DIFF-02); a fifth state Skinned (an .md5mesh: nothing drawn, K41, D127); the time test is binaryModelTimeAccepted (M-MODEL-03), the GLMB tail readGlmbTail (M-MODEL-04); a surface keeps its id, mirroredVerts and dupVerts, a record pendingLoader (gone in LP7.1b: ASE and LWO have their loaders) and its Source materials (P7.22)

§3.7 (LP1c.1), not in the engine: the area counts of the files that exist must agree: the grid names each area once and as many areas as the tree has, every SH probe's area is -1 or below the count; a mismatch drops the grid and the probes (no-bake behaviour) with the reason, and keeps the tree (the newest dmap's). A file that does not parse (dmap or a bake writing it) counts as no file, where the engine stops the map load at its Error; the parse thread probes the files of every bake it holds each poll and reads a changed bake again, so it is retried on the next change. A binary grid that does not parse falls back to the text LP1c fix (S3.12): an SH probe outside the area range drops the probes alone (shProbesError), not the grid; LP1c fix (S3 Low): a text grid's points are appended as they parse, so a count the text cannot hold allocates nothing; LP1c fix (S3.13): a bake read that throws answers its ticket with a slot that says why; K29 (LP4.3): SinkBroom's own rule, the engine cross-checks nothing: it keeps what matches by index and defaults the rest silently, and a grid area at or past the area count is a fatal load error; the preview drops the grid and the probes with the reason on the status line (bake: dropped (<reason>), D90), and the tree stays in use (K16); the grid table is then empty and every surface takes the probe path (black without probes)

entries.note: LP1c.2 (§3.5, R5.6, C7): 1035 of the file's 1404 lines, in 5 ranges, each preceded by one marker line. The imageLoaders table dispatches png and jpg to LoadSTB_RGBA8, tga to LoadTGA, exr to LoadEXR and hdr to LoadHDR; all four and their helpers are copied, so no entry is stubbed. R_LoadImage replaces the shim's transcription of its time-only path (LP1c.1's M-IMG-01) and R_LoadCubeImages the transcribed cube path (M-IMG-02): their time-only paths are the engine's own and stay probe-only, because every loader's ReadFile( name, NULL, timestamp ) reaches the source's probe (M-ID-FN-27, M-FS-08); the cache-name tests prove it. Left out: lines 39-42 (stb_image_write, which no copied range calls), jpg_Error and jpg_Printf (never called), R_WriteTGA, R_WritePNG and R_WriteEXR (M-IMG-NC-01)

LP1c.2: tinyexr.h puts its embedded miniz v1.15 in namespace tinyexr::miniz but declares its functions extern "C", so their linker names (mz_inflate, tinfl_decompress, ...) clash with the miniz TrenchBroom links (LNK2005 in every executable that links TbFsLib). The copied Image_files.cpp is therefore compiled inside shim/src/ShimImageFiles.cpp, which first includes shim/TinyexrMinizNames.h: one macro per external function of the embedded miniz (67 names, the archive ones compiled out but listed), each to tbLitExr_<name>. Only linker names change; the code and its results are the engine's. The engine itself links no other miniz. ShimImageFiles.cpp also defines STBI_NO_THREAD_LOCALS before the copy: stb_image's failure reason and its three per-thread load flags become plain statics, where the engine keeps them thread-local; the executables' static TLS block stays as it was (Release raw data 0x273C), and every load runs on the parse thread (C20), so nothing races on them

LP1c.2: the writers (SinkBroom writes no image, D11's spirit) and the image functions neither the copied loaders nor the fallback's Load2DFromMemory/LoadCubeFromMemory mirrors call. Image.h's copied range 680-699 declares several of them; nothing calls them, so nothing links them

entries.afterReturn: the image type is neither 2, 3 nor 10: neither decoder runs, so the R_StaticAlloc'ed picture is returned uninitialised (and flipped when the attribute bit says so). Unreachable: the loader pre-validation (M-IMG-GUARD-01) refuses the file before LoadTGA or LoadHDR reads it unless the image type is 2, 3 or 10 (tgaProblem)

the colour map is not skipped: the decoder reads the colour map's bytes as pixels, and the image data past them runs off the buffer's end. Unreachable: the loader pre-validation (M-IMG-GUARD-01) refuses the file before LoadTGA or LoadHDR reads it unless the colour map type is 0 (tgaProblem)

the size check uses pixel_size >> 3; the uncompressed loop reports 298 per pixel without advancing, the RLE loop 337/389 per packet, so the picture keeps uninitialised or stale pixels. Unreachable: the loader pre-validation (M-IMG-GUARD-01) refuses the file before LoadTGA or LoadHDR reads it unless the pixel size is 24 or 32, or 8, 24 or 32 for a grey image (tgaProblem)

the decoder reads numBytes from a buffer that holds fewer: it reads past the end of the file's buffer. Unreachable: the loader pre-validation (M-IMG-GUARD-01) refuses the file before LoadTGA or LoadHDR reads it unless the declared size fits the bytes after the header and comment (tgaProblem)

reported once per pixel; neither the read nor the write pointer moves, so the pixel stays uninitialised and the rest of the row shifts. Unreachable: the loader pre-validation (M-IMG-GUARD-01) refuses the file before LoadTGA or LoadHDR reads it unless the pixel size is one the uncompressed decoder reads (tgaProblem)

the run writes the previous packet's colour packetSize times. Unreachable: the loader pre-validation (M-IMG-GUARD-01) refuses the file before LoadTGA or LoadHDR reads it unless the run-length decoder only meets 24 or 32 bits (tgaProblem)

the pixel is not written but counted, so it stays uninitialised. Unreachable: the loader pre-validation (M-IMG-GUARD-01) refuses the file before LoadTGA or LoadHDR reads it unless the run-length decoder only meets 24 or 32 bits (tgaProblem)

frees tinyexr's message and returns without a picture; R_LoadImage tries the other extensions. The file's buffer is not freed on this path (M-IMG-DEFECT-01). Reachable only for a file that passes the pre-validation (M-IMG-GUARD-01: tinyexr's header parse, one channel or R, G and B, a scanline image's offset table and blocks inside the file) and whose data tinyexr then refuses (a corrupt compressed block, a tiled file cut short)

with a picture of 1 or 2 channels (a non-Radiance file stb_image loads as LDR) the conversion reads 3 floats per pixel past the end of stb's buffer; with no picture numChannels is read uninitialised. Unreachable: the loader pre-validation (M-IMG-GUARD-01) refuses the file before LoadTGA or LoadHDR reads it unless the file must be a Radiance HDR whose header and scanlines stb_image reads to the end (hdrProblem), and stb_image always gives such a file three channels

entries.note: LoadEXR returns after a failed LoadEXRFromMemory without Mem_Free( fbuffer ): the file's buffer leaks once per such file and load. Kept verbatim (C7); the pre-validation makes it rare, and the shim's buffers are plain Mem_Alloc blocks

entries.reason: a constant-initialised table of extensions and function pointers, and its count; never written

stb_image's globals are constant-initialised and, with STBI_NO_THREAD_LOCALS (M-IMG-BUILD-01), process-wide: the failure reason is written by each failing call; the flip, unpremultiply and iPhone-conversion flags and the gamma and scale are written only by their setter functions, which nothing calls. Every load runs on the parse thread (C20), so the one writer is that thread LP1c fix (S1.5): the unpremultiply and iPhone flags are at stb_image.h:6380-6418, listed now
a non-const float[256] initialised from literals (constant initialisation), only read by R_MipMapWithGamma; the cmft tables of 854-1167 are static const

entries.note: LP1c.2 (D51, R5.3, C17): every file a copied loader reads is validated outside the copied code before the loader sees it. The file system, between beginImageReads and endImageReads (MaterialDecls::loadImagePixels), reads it through the source's readGameFile and hands the loader nothing (-1, no buffer, FILE_NOT_FOUND_TIMESTAMP) for a file that fails, keeping the refusal once per path; a stop reads every image file as missing, never as an empty buffer. The checks follow each loader's reads: TGA - the 18-byte header, type 2, 3 or 10, no colour map, 24 or 32 bits (8 too for grey), the declared size of an uncompressed image against the bytes after the header and comment, the RLE packets walked as the decoder walks them up to the last pixel; PNG - stb_image's header rules (signature, a 13-byte IHDR first, depth 1/2/4/8/16, colour type 0/2/3/4/6, 16-bit palettes refused, methods 0, interlace 0 or 1, PLTE before IDAT for a palette, unknown critical chunks), every chunk inside the file up to IEND, and the declared pixels within 1032 bytes per IDAT byte (deflate's limit); JPG - SOI, every marker segment inside the file, a baseline or progressive 8-bit frame of 1, 3 or 4 components with sampling 1-4 and tables 0-3, each scan's entropy-coded bytes walked to the next marker, EOI reached, and at most 8 blocks per scan byte (a block of the finest component costs at least one Huffman bit); EXR - tinyexr's ParseEXRVersionFromMemory and ParseEXRHeaderFromMemory, single part and not deep, one channel or R, G and B (what LoadEXRFromMemory needs), for a scanline image the offset table and every block inside the file; HDR - stb_image's identifier, header with FORMAT=32-bit_rle_rgbe, '-Y h +X w' line, and every pixel byte stb_image reads (flat, run-length scanlines, the flat fallback), so stb_image always decodes it to three channels. Every size: at least 1, at most 16384 a side and 8192 x 8192 in all (M-IMG-DIFF-04). An empty file fails. Tested with truncated, 16-bit, RLE-garbage and oversized TGAs, a PNG with a lying IHDR, a 0-byte file and JPGs cut short or with a 4096 x 4096 header over one block of scan data (tst_ImageFiles.cpp) LP1c fix (S3.3): a .png or .jpg is dispatched by its content as stbi__load_main dispatches it (M-IMG-DIFF-04) LP1c fix (S2.8): readImageFile and the probe path catch everything, so nothing throws through a copied loader (an allocation failure reads the file as missing); ImageReads begins and ends the image reads and the recording around a load, so they end also when it throws

engine.anchor: R_LoadCubeImages, CF_SINGLE with a cube size

entries.note: LP1c.2: R_GenerateCubeMapSideFromSingleImage copies a cross of 4 x 3 sides of the cube size out of the picture without looking at the picture's size, so a picture smaller than that is read past its end. Before the copied R_LoadCubeImages runs for a CF_SINGLE image with a cube size, the picture is loaded as it loads it (R_LoadImageProgram, no usage) and a smaller one is refused: the image is the default, with a warning. The picture is decoded twice for such cubes LP1c fix round 2 (X.1): the check now runs inside the transcribed branch (M-IMG-GUARD-04) on the picture the cube is cut from, so the picture is decoded once

LP1c.2: the pre-validation refuses some files the engine would load: images over 16384 a side or 8192 x 8192 in all (the engine has no limit beyond stb_image's 2^24 and the TGA header's 65535), PNG and JPG files cut short that stb_image decodes from zeros, PNG and JPG headers whose size their data cannot hold, unknown critical PNG chunks are refused as stb_image refuses them. An image whose load met a refused file is the default (one warning per refused file, naming it, and not the engine's 'Couldn't load image'), even when R_LoadImage then found another extension of the same name, because the engine would have read past a buffer or crashed on the refused one. LP1c fix (S3.3): the reason "the engine would have read past a buffer or crashed" holds for TGA (Error sites, unchecked RLE), EXR and HDR (Error) only: stb_image checks every read itself and decodes by content, so a .png or .jpg is checked by what it holds (PNG rules for a PNG signature, JPEG rules for a start-of-image marker, stbi_info_from_memory and the size limits for stb_image's other formats), and a refused .png or .jpg is what stb_image's own failure is in the engine: R_LoadImage goes on to the next extension (png, tga, jpg, exr, hdr), and the image is what it finds; a refused TGA, EXR or HDR still makes the image the default. LP1c fix (S2.4): an EXR or HDR file may declare at most a quarter of the pixels (MaxFloatImageFilePixels, 4096 x 4096), as its decoders hold float planes

LP1c.2 (S14): an image's source as ActuallyLoadImage loads it once its cache is not used: the copied R_LoadCubeImages for CF_NATIVE, CF_CAMERA, CF_QUAKE1, CF_SINGLE and CF_PANORAMA (a failure or a side of 0 warns 'Couldn't load cube image: <name>'), the copied R_LoadImageProgram of the PBR-renamed name with the time call's usage for anything else, CF_NATIVE_HDR included as in the engine (a missing picture warns 'Couldn't load image: <name> : <generated name>'); every file through the loader pre-validation (M-IMG-GUARD-01, -02). The pictures are copied out and freed with Mem_Free as ActuallyLoadImage frees them; six sides of 0 that the engine keeps are freed. A quiet load (the editor-image sizes) keeps the copied code's messages in its result. No cache file is written (D11)

engine.anchor: ActuallyLoadImage, the source load and its DeriveOpts

entries.note: LP1c.2 (S14, D24, A3): the source fallback. Where the engine would binarize (no cache, or one resolveImageCache calls Stale) the copied loaders read the source (M-IMG-08) and the levels are what Load2DFromMemory or LoadCubeFromMemory hands its encoder with image_highQualityCompression 0: the 2D colour conversion (YCoCg through the copied idColorSpace::ConvertRGBToCoCg_Y for CFM_YCOCG_DXT5; the fast normal-map swizzle x -> alpha, red and blue 0 for CFM_NORMAL_DXT5; alpha -> green for CFM_GREEN_ALPHA), DXT5's colour format forced to CFM_DEFAULT when neither, the mip chain through the copied R_MipMapR11G11B10F (BC6H, R11G11B10F), R_MipMapWithGamma (gammaMips) or R_MipMap, each level stored as the engine stores an uncompressed format (RGB565 high byte first, then expanded with the cache reader's Option 1; LUM8/INT8 red, ALPHA, L8A8, RG16F, R11G11B10F, RGBA8 for anything else) or as the encoder's RGBA8 input (DXT1, DXT5) or R11G11B10F input (BC6H: the SSE build encodes it). A cube: no conversion, CFM_DEFAULT, the records in the engine's images[ level * 6 + side ] order. Format, colour format and gamma mips are DeriveOpts' for the usage the time call found (a program's pixel path may turn the usage TD_BUMP afterwards, which changes nothing, as in the engine); the mip count is DeriveOpts' for the picture's size and the key's filter. The result is a CachedImage tagged fromSource, published in the image's slot; MaterialService::image answers Ready (cache), Source (fallback), Generated (intrinsic) or Default. Differences: M-IMG-DIFF-05. D61 (tst_ImageGoldens.cpp): against the caches the engine wrote for the same sources (capture_fixtures.py's touch material lines; the LP1b caches of its dmap and map), the shape (type, size, levels, records in the engine's order, the stored format and colour layout) is equal for all 17, the RGB565 light image byte for byte, and the DXT1 and DXT5 caches, decoded by the test's BC1 and BC3 decoder, within the bound of the engine's fast encoders (the alpha and the normal map's green fitted alone within range / 16 + range / 6 + quantisation; BC1 colours within the block's range plus quantisation, since the fast encoders never flip the bounding box's diagonal); the HDR panoramas' BC6H caches by their headers and level records (no BC6H decoder)

LP1c.2 (D24, D11): the fallback stops before the encoder: no BC1, BC3 or BC6H on the CPU, so its levels are RGBA8 where the cache holds DXT1 or DXT5 blocks and R11G11B10F where it holds BC6H (the engine accepts R11G11B10F for BC6H, SC99); its 2D levels are unpadded, where the engine pads a DXT level with zeros to whole 4 x 4 blocks, and a cube level below 4 x 4 keeps its size, where the engine replicates it into one block and records 4 x 4. It writes no cache file (the engine binarizes and writes one): the image is made again per session and on a source change. Image arrays and packed mip chains (engine-made bakes) and the editor's own image are never made from a source. LPF.0a (K34): an image override's raw pixels go through the same conversion (sourceLevels, M-FEED-02) and are drawn uncompressed the same way, the feed's normal case, until the file is saved, the engine binarizes it and the override is cleared

engine.anchor: idImage::ActuallyLoadImage (the cache's size, the source's, the 8 x 8 default)

entries.note: LP1c.2 (C21, A6, P.4, P.11): MaterialEntry::editorImageSize is GetEditorImage's upload size, measured on the parse thread when the entry is published (sized, LP1b.0's hook), silently (the copied code's messages while it measures are dropped). The chain: qer_editorimage's key as ImageFromFile names and finds it with TF_DEFAULT, TR_REPEAT, TD_DIFFUSE (the default image for an empty or default name, the fonts and lights usages, the extensions stripped, an existing record), without making a record; when its load is defaulted, the first SL_DIFFUSE stage's image or stage 0's when that one has none, but the defaulted editor image when no stage is diffuse; without qer_editorimage the first SL_DIFFUSE stage's image, else stage 0's; no stage or no image: the default image. An image's size: the default image and the fixed-size intrinsics by their generators (16 x 16 for _default, _white, _black, _flat, ...; _quadratic 32 x 4; window-, cvar- and font-sized ones unknown, Default); else the time call names the cache, and a cache the engine would use (not stale, matching DeriveOpts, the BFHACK name too) gives its header's size, read with readGameFileHead (36 bytes, not the body); else the source: a single image's file, the one the copied R_LoadImage's leaf resolution found in the time call (the .tga default, png/tga/jpg/exr/hdr, the _rmao sibling), sized by its header when the loader pre-validation passes it (imageFileHeader); a program or a cube through the copied loaders, quietly (a program by its first leaf; addnormals resamples its second to the first's size); a load that fails or a missing source is the engine's defaulted 8 x 8. Ready is a size the engine uploads; Default is the defaulted 8 x 8 or an unknown size, with the reason. A Ready size is kept per canonical name across reloads (D52). The LP1b fixture's six editor images equal the engine's listImages, from the caches' headers and from the sources' alike (tst_EditorImageSize.cpp)

LP1c.2 (C21): the engine loads an image once per level and again on reloadImages; the preview re-reads on its 1 s poll: the loose files each published editor-image size and each image slot was read from, or that the time call found, are probed (no body read), and one whose time, size or change stamp changed makes the slot read again (resolveImage) and the material's size measured again, its kept Ready size dropped so that the new size or the loss of the file is published under every name that shares the entry. Files in containers are not polled (their tables are read once). A Ready size that changes to another Ready size reaches the chunks only when they are rebuilt for another reason: SceneGeometry rebuilds provisional (Default) chunks when their size turns Ready (a follow-up) LP1c fix (S2.5, S2.7): SceneGeometry keeps the size each material's cells were built with and builds them again on any change of the table's size (Default to Ready, Ready to another Ready, Ready back to Default for a deleted texture); the poll re-probes a slice of at most 5 ms per poll, going on where it stopped, with stop checks; a measure that the poll asks for is queued (M-IMG-DIFF-08)

An intrinsic the engine sizes by its window, a cvar or a font atlas (_currentRender, _shadowMapAtlas, _imguiFont, ...) is Default here. GetEditorImage's record is never made, so listImages-like listings of the registry do not show editor images the engine's dmap would have loaded LP1c fix (S2.2, S3.3): every source size is a header's now (M-IMG-DIFF-08), a program's by its first leaf and a cube's by its sides' headers; a .png or .jpg whose header is refused gives way to the next extension's file, as the engine's loop does

engine.anchor: R_LoadCubeImages, the six-side loop and its error path

entries.note: LP1c fix (S2.1): when R_LoadCubeImages stops at side i (a side missing, which leaves width 0, or of another size) it frees sides 0 to i-1 without nulling them and returns false; a side i it loaded before the size test failed is leaked (the engine's ActuallyLoadImage frees nothing after the false). Kept verbatim (C7). The shim frees nothing after a false return (LP1c.2 freed every non-null side again: a double free, S2.1/S3.1) and frees the six sides only for a loaded cube of size 0; the six sides' headers are checked first (M-IMG-GUARD-03), so the copy is called only for six sides of one size and the leak is unreachable; a side refused by the pre-validation as the copy reads it, or a stop between sides, reads as missing, and the copy frees what it loaded itself LP1c fix round 2 (X.2): the header check does not make the leak unreachable by itself: a side 0 whose header passes but whose body is refused or does not decode leaves width 0, side 1 then fails the size test and is leaked. So side 0 is also decoded whole (the copied R_LoadImageProgram, inside the image reads) before the copy runs, and a side 0 without a picture fails the load; the leak is unreachable unless a side changes on disk between that decode and the copy's LP1c fix round 3 (Y.1): that, too, was not the whole truth: a side's load can find another file than the one whose header was checked (a refused .tga, then a sibling .png of another size), and side 0 decoded alone compared no size. So the pixel path no longer calls the copied loop: the shim runs a transcription of R_LoadCubeImages' six-file part (loadSixFileCube) that also frees the side that stops the loop on its size, and the leak is unreachable on every path. The side-0 decode of round 2 is gone (side 0 is decoded once again); the copy keeps the defect verbatim and runs only for the time call

LP1c fix (S2.1, S2.2): before the copied R_LoadCubeImages reads a six-file cube's pixels (CF_NATIVE, CF_CAMERA, CF_QUAKE1, CF_SINGLE without a cube size), each side's name (R_LoadCubeImages' side tables, transcribed) is resolved by the copied time call (R_LoadImageProgram, no pixels) and its file's header read through the source without its body: a side missing, a header refused or sides of different sizes (side 0 square) fail the load with "Couldn't load cube image" (and the engine's "Mismatched sizes on cube map" for sizes) without the copy. The same check sizes a cube for C21 (side 0's header) without decoding it LP1c fix round 2: side 0 is decoded whole before the copy (X.2, M-IMG-DEFECT-03), and a side whose .png or .jpg header is refused gives way to the next extension of the loader order, as R_LoadImage does after stb_image's failure (X.9) LP1c fix round 3 (Y.1): the header check is now an early refusal (and C21's sizing); the guard against the leak is the transcribed loop (loadSixFileCube), which frees every side it loaded when it fails, the mismatched one included

LP1c fix (S2.2): the engine sizes an editor image when dmap loads it; the preview publishes a material at once with its last Ready size for the same image chain (D52, S3.15) or the registry's Default, unmeasured, and measures it on a low-priority queue (steps of 20 ms) only once a consumer looked it up (the bulk parse measures nothing; a lookup of a bulk-parsed name queues it). The measure never decodes: a usable cache's 36-byte header; else a 2D image or program by its first leaf's header, once the time call found every leaf (a missing leaf ends the copied time call, so its last probe is a miss); a six-file cube by side 0 after M-IMG-GUARD-03; a CF_SINGLE cube by its cube size once the picture's header holds the 4 x 3 sides; a panorama 1024. Headers come through small bounded reads (4 KB, 64 KB, 1 MB; readImageFileHeader), with the header rules and the lengths a header tells; the body of a file (RLE packets, PNG chunks, JPEG scans, EXR blocks) is not walked, so a file the pre-validation refuses by its body has a Ready size here (M-IMG-DIFF-07). A kept Ready size stands for a Default measure only while the files it was measured from are unchanged; a deleted texture returns to Default. LP5.F (D77 as A41 restates it, A6, D18; 43-FLOOR-PROBE-FLAKE.md): a chunk built at the Default size while its slot is unmeasured (Chunk::provisional) is drawn provisionally at 8 x 8 as before, and no frame that draws it is settled: SceneGeometry's sized cells record at apply whether that size is final (a non-provisional chunk, or a measured or Failed slot), waitsForMaterials holds while one is not, and so FrameConvergence::provisionalChunks; a scanned table whose slot is measured at the same size ends the wait without a rebuild (a measured Default is the engine's 8 x 8 for an image it cannot load), another size rebuilds the cells (S2.5). The scan moves the scene's wait state, which triggers the next frame (geometryTick); a bulk-parsed slot is looked up once its wait starts, so its measure is queued. The engine has no such frame: dmap sized every editor image before the map was drawn. LP5.F addendum: a slot published again unmeasured over a measured size (remeasure: an override's new editorSize, D111, or a changed file the poll found) is MaterialSlot::remeasured and moves the table's sizesRevision: its cells wait whatever their size (SizedCells::measured recomputed at every scan) until the measure lands, and are built again at a new size (S2.5); a frame whose table's sizesRevision the scene has not scanned is not settled (geometryInFlight). A kept Ready size (D52) stays final: firstSlot keeps it only for the same image chain, and a rebuild, the poll and an override's change drop it first once its files changed or another size stands, so it is the size a measure would give (short of a file changed unseen: the poll off and no rebuild before a re-parse)

LP1c fix (S2.3, S2.4, S2.5): the engine keeps an image in VRAM once loaded; the preview's parse thread reads images in work items of up to 100 ms (or 256 images; LP4.3: a read batch's containers are reopened per item), each ending after the image in hand once more urgent work is queued (a reload, an evaluation, an image override (LPF.0a), a lookup, a bake, a measure), below the lookups, the measures and the evaluations, and keeps the published images' data within MaterialServiceOptions::imageBudgetBytes (512 MB): beyond it, the least recently published image whose data a consumer has taken (image() returned it) leaves the table and is read again when asked for (about 0.5 ms a cache). A reload drops the image slots whose files changed (LP1c fix round 2, below), so new containers and caches the engine wrote are seen then (materialCollectionsDidChange, or a new session). The source fallback takes the loader's pixels as its working buffer and writes its levels into one buffer reserved for them all (about 1.3 GB less for an 8192 x 8192 source); it stops between levels once the session stops. LP2's upload-and-drop policy and the VRAM budget are LP2's LP1c fix round 2 (X.3): a reload drops only the image slots whose files the new source finds otherwise (a file found or missed, the cache's name included, a container entry's kind and container) and slots with no file; an unchanged slot keeps its pointer, so an .mtr save reads no image again. (X.11) A slot the poll drops is no longer counted as taken. (X.4, recorded) An evaluation waits at most for the work item in flight, which is one image (the batch ends after it) or one bake: a source decode costs about 39 ms per 1024 x 1024 PNG in Release (the retail materialorb sources), so up to about 2.5 s at the 8192 x 8192 cap (D51), more in Debug; LP2's requests should ask small images first or bound a decode per item

LP1c fix (S2.2): the engine opens a loose file by trying it; the preview lists each loose folder it looks in once and keeps its names (folded as the file system compares them), so a file that is not there costs a lookup, not a file-system call. looseFilesMayHaveChanged (the parse thread's 1 s poll) starts a round: the first look into a folder after it stats the folder and lists it again when its time changed. A file added after its folder was listed is seen at the next poll (the poll's re-probe then reads what missed it again, M-IMG-DIFF-03); a changed file is seen by its own stat as before. A .resources container is statted once when a read batch opens it, not per read: a container replaced during one batch is read through the handle the batch opened, and refused from the next LP1c fix round 2 (X.10): a folder whose time is within 2 s of its listing is listed again at each new round, so a file added within the same tick of a coarse file-system clock (FAT, exFAT, HFS+, some network shares) is not missed LP1c fix round 3 (Y.3): a folder whose time lies ahead of the clock (a share's skew) is not "recent": it is listed once, and again only when its time changes

NVRHI checks neither the heap's memory type nor an image's dedicated requirement (P8.3), so the session probes every format class at its first frame (vkGetImageMemoryRequirements2 with VkMemoryDedicatedRequirements through its dispatcher, against the first DEVICE_LOCAL type createHeap takes)

LP2.0 (D9, C3, C26, P2.19): the engine creates its programs from the blobs without looking into them; the preview reflects every shader it loads with SPIRV-Reflect (the pin SPIRV-Reflect) and compares it with the mirrored tables: every descriptor (set, Vulkan binding = slot + NVRHI's offset, type) is in the program's binding layouts; a push-constant block only where the layout pushes, and of the table's size; the constant block's members (a cbuffer holding one struct is taken as that struct) by name and offset, their count and the block's size against the renderparm set or the pass's struct; a vertex shader's inputs (built-ins left out) at the vertex layout's locations with the component counts of the engine's VS_IN. A shader may leave out what the layout has. A mismatch disables the program with a message naming the field (D9); the hidden retail test reflects all 30 permutations of LP2's ten programs (pushed and not) equal to the tables. Code shorter than SPIR-V's header is refused before SPIRV-Reflect reads it (it reads the generator word unchecked). LP5.0: the hidden retail cases also reflect rows 15, 17, 18, 21, 22, 55, 57, 65, 67, 69 and 70 (44 permutations) and the twelve material programs (48) equal to the tables, the sets member by member

LP2.0 (D71, C3): a pipeline is keyed as the engine keys it (state bits, program, int depth bias, slope bias, framebuffer) with the framebuffer as its colour and depth formats (NVRHI's FramebufferInfo compares formats and sample counts only), plus the recipe: Draw is GetOrCreatePipeline (TriangleList, scissor, depth test and write, blend on all targets, then the copied GetRenderState, M-PIPE-PURE-01), its input layout LAYOUT_DRAW_VERT made against the vertex shader; Tonemap is TonemapPass's (TriangleStrip, no culling, depth and stencil off); Blit is CommonPasses' (rect.vs with blit.ps TEXTURE_ARRAY=0, TriangleStrip, no culling, depth and stencil off, the default disabled blend). Compute pipelines are TonemapPass's histogram and exposure ({CS, the one layout}). Shaders are cached per (name, stage, permutation key); binding layouts per (layout type, pushed)

engine.anchor: idRenderProgManager::Init, the builtins loaded at start

entries.note: LP2.0 (D71, D42, D9, R4-2.21): the engine loads every builtin's shaders at start and makes a pipeline on its render thread at first use, against the live framebuffer the key points to. The preview makes shaders, layouts and pipelines lazily on its compile thread (a StackThread of 8 MB, P2.27), against 1x1 format-only framebuffers of its own, one per format set; a request returns Pending at once and the made pipeline triggers a frame (D77). No pipeline cache file is read or written (D42). A missing blob or permutation, or a reflection mismatch, disables the program for the session with the field named and one warning, where the engine calls FatalError LP2 fix round: T0.8: an NVRHI Error raised on the compile thread (the validation wrapper's message, or a driver failure NVRHI reports) reaches the device's message callback and ends the session; a key is Failed only for a disabled program or a null pipeline without a message; in Debug a failing vkCreateGraphicsPipelines asserts inside NVRHI (ASSERT_VK_OK). T0.7: a Stop is seen before each creation step (a shader, the binding layouts, the input layout, the framebuffer, the pipeline), so it waits for at most one driver call; the stopped job's key stays Pending and disables nothing. DX.5: at Start (phase B) a session with an absolute game path asks for the eleven pipelines every lit scene draws with (depth at state 0 and with GLS_ALPHAMASK, the solid draw of a surface whose registers are pending (round 2, V2.7), texture_color at state 0, interaction and PBR interaction with EQUAL and LESS, tonemapping, the blit, histogram and exposure), where the engine makes each at its first draw.

engine.anchor: LoadProgram, the input layout of every LAYOUT_DRAW_VERT program

entries.note: LP2.0: every LAYOUT_DRAW_VERT program gets the full input layout (locations 0 to 5), while its vertex shader reads fewer (depth.vs and color.vs location 0; texture_color.vs 0, 1 and 4; interaction.vs 0 to 4, the retail test prints them). NVRHI numbers attribute locations densely, so no layout can leave out 2 and 3 for texture_color without changing NVRHI; the preview keeps the engine's layout, and Vulkan's validation layer reports a warning "Vertex attribute at location N not consumed by vertex shader" per attribute, as for the engine under r_useValidationLayers. The [litgpu] pipeline tests count these apart; every other validation message is 0

U2.3 (31-LP2-FIXES.md), the first recorded deviation from the NVRHI pin (Q14's wording): at 3d81b755 UploadManager::CreateChunk maps the buffer createBuffer returned without looking at it, and createBuffer returns null when the buffer's memory cannot be allocated (CHECK_VK_FAIL) and leaks the Buffer and its VkBuffer; writeTexture ignores suballocateBuffer's result. A full device or host heap therefore crashed the process inside NVRHI. The CPM patch makes CreateChunk report an Error through the device's message callback (which ends a SinkBroom session) and return no chunk, suballocateBuffer return false, writeTexture and writeBuffer return when it does, and createBuffer destroy the Buffer whose memory failed. Tested with a hook that fails every host-only allocation (GpuDevice failHostAllocationsForTesting): the session ends with "NVRHI error: Failed to create an upload chunk buffer", every allocation freed

engine.anchor: TonemapPass::Init, the histogram and exposure buffers

entries.note: LP2.1 step 2 (C6, C14, SC254-SC256, SC261): _currentRenderHDR RGBA16_FLOAT (render target, and UAV as the engine's one-sample image), _currentDepth TD_DEPTH_STENCIL through AllocImage's format map (D24S8 where the device has it, else D32S8; DepthWrite, clear value 1), _currentRenderLDR RGBA8_UNORM (TD_LOOKUP_TABLE_RGBA), each 2D with one level and one sample, keepInitialState, clear value 0; ldrFBO {LDR, depth} and hdrFBO {HDR, depth}; HistogramBuffer (256 bins) and ExposureBuffer (1) as R32_UINT typed UAVs kept in UnorderedAccess. The preview sizes them to its surface (headless: the headless extent), not renderSystem's window, and makes them again on a size change with the render-target generation bumped (C28); the engine's ResizeFramebuffers deletes and makes the framebuffers likewise. The replaced targets are held until their frame has finished (a clear holds no NVRHI reference)

LP2.1 step 2 (D70, SC261): the engine never clears its exposure buffer (ResetExposure has no caller), so its first frame adapts from whatever the allocation held; the preview clears it to 0 once at Start, in the first frame's command list before any pass, so that every session starts from the same value. In the engine's steady state, tens of seconds after start, the difference is gone (K24)

engine.anchor: idRenderBackend::Init, the command list's upload chunk size

entries.note: LP2.1 step 3 (S8, D36, D78): the engine appends a level's static geometry to one fixed static vertex and index buffer (FatalError when full) and never frees a range until the level unloads; the preview edits the map live, so its chunks live in 64 MB vertex and index arenas with a range allocator whose freed ranges are reused only once the frame that freed them has finished, another arena of the kind added when none holds a chunk, and at most 32 MB uploaded per frame (the rest waits; the frame is unconverged, D77). The render thread's command list uses 32 MB upload chunks; the engine's r_vkUploadBufferSizeMB is 64. The vertex layout (idDrawVert, C4) and the 16-bit indexes are the engine's U2.9 (LP2 fix round, deferred to LP6's compaction): arenas never shrink before teardown, and a rebuild of more than an arena's free space cannot reuse its own freed ranges in that frame (a material reload changes every appearanceVersion), so another arena of the kind is added and stays: up to twice the geometry plus 64 MB per kind (admin stayed at 2 x 64 MB); GpuMemoryAccount counts it in arenaBytes.

LP2.1 step 4 (C28, P2.14d): the engine loads every image of a level before it draws (ActuallyLoadImage writes the whole image in one command list), so it never binds a stand-in; the preview loads images while it draws, so a slot whose texture has not arrived, and one the service has no image for (Default), binds its usage's intrinsic: TD_BUMP _flat, TD_LIGHT (falloff and projection images) _white, every other usage _default. A settled frame (D77) has every visible texture at its full mips, so the stand-in never reaches a parity shot. LPF.1 (C40, D98): a slot asked again for a changed image while it holds a complete texture keeps binding that texture until the new one is complete (Replacing, M-FEED-DIFF-05), so a replacement shows no stand-in either

engine.anchor: LoadEXR, the packing of the float picture to R11G11B10F

entries.note: LPF.0a (C39 (a), P5.5): an RGBA32F override (TD_HDRI and TD_HDR_LIGHTPROBE only) is packed as LoadEXR packs its picture: each texel's first three floats through the copied float3_to_r11g11b10f (M-IMG-COPY-03) into one uint32_t in the machine's byte order, the alpha dropped; the loop is transcribed in the shim (a memcpy for the engine's pointer casts) and runs on the parse thread inside the Feed work item (C20). The packed picture then goes through the source fallback's conversion as a loaded EXR does (M-FEED-02)

entries.note: LPF.0a (C39, D97, P5.1, P5.6): an override's slot for one key: the copied time call (MaterialDecls::imageCacheName, M-IMG-03) names the cache and gives the usage and texture type, the one file probe an override makes; then (a) raw pixels convert through sourceLevels, the source fallback's conversion shared with sourceImage (sourceImageLevels with DeriveOpts for name.usage, never key.usage, the mip count for the picture's size and the key's filter, RGB565 expanded: M-IMG-DIFF-05), RGBA8 for every usage but TD_HDRI and TD_HDR_LIGHTPROBE, RGBA32F for those only (M-FEED-01), the cross pairs refused; (b) GPU-ready levels are taken as they are when they pass the test a .bimage passes (engineCacheMatches: the usage's colour format, its format or that format's uncompressed twin, RGBA8 for RGB565 and R11G11B10F for BC6H, the key's texture type, so 6 faces exactly for a cube key), have the binarizer's records (numLevels x faces, level-major, each record's level, side and halved size) and pass the upload's engineTextureDesc and levelUploadBytes; D24: their compression is the caller's. A level beyond UploadBytesPerFrame over all its faces is refused (M-TEX-DIFF-02). The slot is Ready, marked override, with the time call's name (its usage is what the draws read) and no files
