entries.note: LPF.0a (C39, C40, D96, D97, P5.1, P5.16): the engine reads an image's files at load (ActuallyLoadImage); the preview also takes an image from a host in memory, under a game image name, in place of its files, without writing one (C8): MaterialService::setImageOverride, one Feed work item per name, served after the evaluations and ahead of the lookups, the newest hand-over winning. The matching rule is ImageFromFile's: the override's name folded as the engine folds a name before it compares it with its records (every .tga, .jpg, .png, .exr and .hdr removed wherever it stands, case-sensitively as idStr::Replace compares, so an upper-case extension stays; backslashes made slashes), then compared without case with a key's whole name (a record's name, folded already). A program key (addnormals( ... ), heightmap( ... )) is the record of its whole program text, so it matches only by that text, never by a leaf: an override of textures/foo_local does not feed bumpmap addnormals( textures/foo_local, ... ). The default image (an empty name, "default") and the built-ins (a name that starts with '_', which match any options and are never read from files) are refused at hand-over. The usage the override converts with is the copied time call's for each key (M-FEED-02): a stage naming <x>_rmao is TD_SPECULAR_PBR_RMAO at parse (Material.cpp), and an <x>_s key becomes it only when the <x>_rmao sibling file exists, as in the engine, so a host without files reaches the RMAO path by naming _rmao. Two usages of one name are two keys, two slots and two conversions. A set publishes the keys' drops and their new slots in one table, a refusal and a clear one table too (the clear reads the files in the same item); MaterialTable::feedApplied counts the hand-overs a table includes against MaterialService::feedRequested (D100). imageItem's break test gains the Feed queue (LP4.3's batching, named for the end review: P5.21). LPF.0b (C42, D96, D99, P5.8, P5.18): the preview also takes a material's decl text from a host (MaterialService::reparseMaterial, one Reparse work item per name, served after the overrides and ahead of the lookups, the newest text winning, counted in feedApplied); the engine parses a decl again only through its editors' SetText and Invalidate, or reloadDecls (ReloadFile, which re-reads the files). The re-parse is the editors' path (M-ID-FN-28); the text is kept by the service and applied again after every registry build, since a build reads the decl files again, until clearMaterialReparse. A re-parsed name without a decl stays an implicit decl (IsImplicit: its sourceFile is the implicit file), so FindMaterial( name, false ), the preview's findMaterialNoDefault, takes it for none and a light whose texture names it gets the default light shader unless the texture was precached. The slot is set under the asked name, the canonical name and every name the material was published under (a Failed lookup's names recorded too); a refused text or an engine Error publishes it Failed, where the engine would have stopped. The material's register deltas are erased (they are evaluated again when asked), where the engine evaluates the registers every frame. LPF.1 (C44, D100, D101; P5.2, P5.13, P5.20): the engine takes a file's change only at a load (the map's, reloadImages, reloadDecls), never while it draws, so nothing counts what a frame includes; the preview's frames follow the feed: a frame is settled only when the table it refreshed with at its start holds every hand-over the service had counted when it converged (feedApplied == feedRequested, FrameConvergence::feedBehind; not a re-trigger term) and the scene has scanned that table's materialsRevision (a re-parse's cells), so no read-back shows the state before a queued change; the idle pass's feedTick triggers a frame at once when a feed publication the last frame did not refresh with changed a slot or a material, or the last frame was behind the feed (no 100 ms arrival coalescing; the 30 Hz pacer stands, so a 10 ms feeder draws at most 30 frames a second); a refusal, an override of a name no slot uses or a clear of nothing changes nothing drawn and draws no frame in a settled session. Every publication's tableChanged wakes the loop for another idle pass, which reads the moved counter whatever the slots' states (19-LITGPU-HANG.md's rule). The frame log gains feed_applied (the frame's table's counter), feed_ms (from an item's newest hand-over, carried in the table's feed records, to the first presented frame whose table includes it and in which its slots are Resident with every level written, or for a re-parse its lists were built with its materialsRevision and its cells built; the largest of the items landing in one frame; empty on other frames; a newer item takes over an older one's slots, and an item with no slot and no revision, a refusal, lands nowhere) and override_bytes (the store's bytes): 49 columns; the engine's bytes to pixels has no counterpart. LPF.2 (D107, D108): the host API has no engine counterpart (the engine reads its map and files at load and draws into its own window): a Qt-free host makes the instance (M-INST-02), the material service with a guarded listener that calls tableChanged on the parse thread and is detached before the render thread stops, the session (headless or on its surface), snapshot records from the builders or a map text (lexerFloat reads, the brush polygons by a double-precision plane solve, exact for axial float-exact brushes), and reads the LDR target of the first settled frame back (settled includes the feed's counters, so a host that keeps feeding gets the timeout's reason); the teardown helper runs LitSessionHost's order; FEED.md is the contract LP5.G (D18; C44's rule generalised to every table publication): the engine draws every frame, so a reloadDecls is on screen at the next one; the preview draws on a trigger, and a material reload in a settled session drew none until the camera moved: a registry build (reload(), the poll's changed decl file) moves neither materialsRevision nor sizesRevision, only the table's registry, and the scene builds every cell again, byte-identical where nothing moved them, so the arenas queue no upload and geometryTick does not trigger (litTableTick fires only while the passes wait for a table, feedTick only for a feed publication). The trigger rules themselves never covered it: from LP2.4 to LP4.3 the admin measurement's reload drew its frame only because every build gave the patchDef3 chunks other bytes (uninitialised normals, M-GEO-DEFECT-01), which 12eb8c1a0 made deterministic. The idle pass's tableTick, after feedTick (unchanged), triggers a frame at once (no arrival clock; the pacer still spaces frame starts) when the newest table's registry, materialsRevision or sizesRevision differs from the table the last frame refreshed with and the scene's scan gave the scene work: its wait state moved since that frame in the terms before the scanned revisions (applied batches, busy, the bake, an entityDef, a measure, the probes and their table), so a scan that only took a revision draws nothing; that frame is unconverged while the work runs and geometryTick's DX.4 trigger draws the one that settles. A lookup and the poll with no change move no key and draw nothing (the admin measurement: 0 frames in 20 s idle with the poll on). A build always gives work (V.2: every cell marked), so a changed decl file draws frames even for a material not in view. H.1: each publication's tableChanged wakes the loop; the pass reads the newest table after geometryTick adopted it (a batch in flight adopts it at its end, polled while building) and runs again for one published meanwhile. LP5.G addendum (D18, D77): a texture saved again from a paint program at the same size was not redrawn until the camera moved: the poll's re-probe drops the image and publishes a table whose imageChanges moved, which is no feed item (feedTick keys on feedApplied) and moves no table key (tableTick), and arrivalsTick looked for arrivals only while a slot was pending, which none is until a frame asks the slot again; a different size drew only when the file was also the material's editor image (the remeasure moves sizesRevision). arrivalsTick now first reads the newest table: when its imageChanges differs from the table the last frame refreshed with and a key changed since then (changedImages) has a slot on the render side, it triggers a frame at once (no arrival clock; the pacer still spaces frame starts); that frame's refreshImages asks the slot again, which keeps its texture bound (Replacing, unconverged), and the new image's publication is an arrival. A change of an image nothing draws draws nothing. H.1: every idle pass reads the newest table until a frame has refreshed with it, and the drop's tableChanged wakes the loop for that pass, so no re-saved file is waited past.

LPF.0a (C41, D99, P5.7, P5.19): the override store in the material service's parse thread (never the shim: C17) is the truth, a published slot its derivative: override slots stay across builds through dropChangedImages' skip alone (no re-apply, no conversion at a build); they are not exempt from the image budget (S2.4, M-IMG-DIFF-09): a taken one may be dropped and is converted from the store again when asked for; lookUpImage consults the store before C8's search, so a key first asked for after the hand-over is converted at its first lookup. The poll never probes an overridden key's files (its slot has none); the copied time call that names an override's cache and gives its usage (its probes of the _rmao sibling and of a program's leaves) is the one probe an override makes. A key the store's image is refused for at its first lookup (a usage the pixels do not fit) is read from its files, its status Refused. Without a registry (a failed build) nothing converts: the override waits Pending, its keys answer the build's failure, and the next build's dropChangedImages drops those slots, so the consumers' lookups convert it. MaterialTable::overrideBytes is the store's bytes, the converted slots counting in the budget's

LPF.0a (D111, K36, P5.7): the engine sizes an editor image from its files alone; an override may carry an editorSize, which stands for its image's files in C21's size chain (editorImageSize's sizeOverride: Ready, not defaulted, nothing probed), so a host without files does not tile its material by the 8 x 8 default. A set or clear whose editorSize changes remeasures every published material whose image chain holds the name (a name -> materials index filled as materials are measured, beside the size files), whose kept Ready size goes first, so a clear brings the files' size back; SceneGeometry::scanTable's size rule rebuilds their cells as for any size change. LP5.F addendum: the remeasure an override's new editorSize starts publishes the slot unmeasured at the old size, MaterialSlot::remeasured, and moves MaterialTable::sizesRevision; until the measure lands no frame is settled (the scene's cells of the material wait, SceneGeometry::waitsForMaterials, and the frame whose table the scene has not scanned is geometryInFlight), so readbackLdr never shows the old UVs under the new image (tst_Feed.cpp: 8 x 1 stripes at 512, then 256 with the measures held: no settled frame, then the new UVs)

LP2.1 step 5 (SC265-SC268, P2.14c/e): an image of the cache's shape becomes the texture AllocImage makes: the format map (engineTextureFormat, M-TABLE), the component mapping (engineComponentMapping), Texture2D or TextureCube with 6 slices (DTT_2D_ARRAY a Texture2DArray of 6), numLevels levels, a compressed image's size rounded up to whole 4 x 4 blocks (473-477); every level record is written with writeTexture(texture, destZ, level, bytes, GetRowPitch(format, width)) and the texture ends ShaderResource with setPermanentTextureState and commitBarriers (890-891). RGB565 caches arrive as RGBA8 (the cache reader's expansion, as BinaryImage expands them), source images in the engine's layouts as RGBA8 or R11G11B10F (D24): nothing is converted on the render thread. Not as the engine: the texture is not allocated through VMA (one NVRHI allocation each, D72), it is created with ShaderResource as its kept initial state instead of being tracked from Common, and its levels may arrive over several frames (M-TEX-DIFF-01). The cache's BC levels are unpadded, so the pitch is exactly one block row; an image whose level holds fewer bytes than its rows need, or whose format has no NVRHI format or pitch (BC7, ETC1), makes its slot Default with the reason

LP2.1 step 5 (§3.10, D78, P2.14c): the engine writes every level of an image in one command list before it draws; the preview writes the smallest levels first, a level (all six sides of a cube's) at a time, within the frame's 32 MB upload cap (a level larger than the cap goes alone as its frame's first upload), and binds the texture through an SRV subresource range of the written levels only, never an unwritten one; each extension of the range bumps the slot's version, so the binding sets that hold it are made again. A settled frame (D77) has every visible texture at its full mips

U3.16 (31-LP2-FIXES.md): the engine writes every level whole; a level (all its sides) larger than UploadBytesPerFrame (32 MB) would be one writeTexture through one upload chunk of its own size (a 16384 x 16384 RGBA8 level: 1 GiB), so the preview refuses the image: its slot is Default, with the reason, and binds its usage's intrinsic. LPF.0a (D103, P5.6, P5.25): the material service refuses an image override with such a level when its Feed item converts it, with the same UploadBytesPerFrame (the render side's constant; setUploadCapForTesting does not move it) and the level's bytes summed over all its faces (levelUploadBytes): a raw RGBA8 2D side above 2896, a raw RGBA8 cube side above 1182; the reason names this entry, the slots stand (Q27: larger images come as GPU-ready levels or downsampled)

U2.3 (31-LP2-FIXES.md): the engine makes a texture whenever it loads an image; the preview makes no new texture or geometry arena once the live device allocations come within AllocationHeadroom (64) of maxMemoryAllocationCount, so that NVRHI's upload chunks and staging can still allocate (D72: about one allocation per texture): the slot stays at its intrinsic, an arena's chunk stays queued (its draws skipped, the frame unconverged), the session warns once and the frame log's alloc_refused column counts them. LPF.1 (D102): a Replacing slot whose new texture the headroom refuses keeps its complete texture bound and its image for a later frame, counted once until its texture is made (M-FEED-DIFF-05). LP6.4a (C68 (a), the director's reading (1)): the headroom guards device allocations only, a dedicated texture or a new texture heap; a texture that fits a heap's free range makes no allocation and is never refused for it (the frame log's texture_heaps, heap_bytes and textures_dedicated beside alloc_count)

LP2.1 (T0.14 of 29-LP2-0-REVIEW.md): the copied GetRowPitch calls BitsForFormat, whose default case asserts in Debug and returns 0 in Release for a format outside textureFormat_t, and FMT_NONE gives 0 too; a zero pitch makes NVRHI's writeTexture copy nothing (nvrhi rule 12). The facade refuses a format outside FMT_RGBA8 to FMT_RGBA16S, FMT_NONE, a width below 1 and a zero pitch (nullopt) before the copy runs, and the uploader makes such an image's slot Default with the reason

entries.note: LP2.1 step 6 (D69, D24): a DXT5 level of one colour as the engine's fast SSE2 encoders write it (DXTEncoder_SSE2.cpp at 285ea4d1, the test-only copy M-IMG-DXT-*: CompressImageDXT5Fast, CompressYCoCgDXT5Fast with ScaleYCoCg, InsetYCoCgBBox, SelectYCoCgDiagonal and EmitCoCgIndices, CompressNormalMapDXT5Fast with InsetNormalsBBoxDXT5, EmitAlphaIndices and EmitGreenIndices), by their lane arithmetic for one colour: no encoder runs in the product. tst_IntrinsicImages compares every level of the seven LP2 intrinsics with the copied encoder: byte-equal

entries.note: K28 (31-LP2-FIXES.md, replacing DX.1; restated in round 2 from 32-LP2-VERIFY.md V2.1): dmap runs OptimizeEntity on every area by default, which throws away each coplanar group's side triangles and builds them again (BuildOptTriangles, RegenerateTriangles) from candidate edges sorted by an unstable qsort (equal lengths tie, as a rectangle's two diagonals do), so the .proc's triangles are not fans of the side windings (the parity .proc: 96 of 110 pairs of the (a b c)(d c b) shape); copying the optimizer would import the CRT's qsort tie order. The preview keeps its own triangulation (K9's family). The mechanism by which this changes pixels: the interaction vertex shader writes the normalised vector to the viewer per vertex in tangent space (interaction.vs.hlsl:193-200), the rasteriser interpolates it over the triangle, and the pixel shader normalises it again (interaction.ps.hlsl:98) and reads it in the view-dependent normal contrast before the Lambert term (:112-121) and in the half vector and the BRDF (:138-139, :181-183). A per-vertex normalised vector interpolated over a triangle depends on the triangle: the same face cut along the other diagonal gives another per-pixel view vector (4-17 degrees apart on large triangles near the camera, measured from the .proc's triangles). So bump-mapped and specular pixels differ wherever a triangle is large against its distance from the camera: |d| <= 4 on R05 (941 pixels beyond 1), <= 2 on R18 (28), masked <= 17 at texel edges on R08, R09 and R12's ceilings, |d| = 1 on 0.01-3 % of every bump-mapped row, and up to 12 where a triangle crosses the near plane (R05b: 2,568 unmasked pixels from 2 to 12, 9,950 at 1, masked max 7; the same on the LP2.3 run and the fix round's). A flat normal and no specular stage do not take the view vector out (V3.1, 32-LP2-VERIFY.md, corrected in LP4.1): without a specular stage the engine zeroes the specular colour (RenderBackend.cpp:2151 clears inter.specularColor, :1156-1158 binds _black for a missing specular image, :1190 writes the zero SPECULARMODIFIER), so the BRDF's specular term and its Fresnel_Schlick( 0, vdotH ) contribute nothing; the view vector reaches these pixels through the view-dependent normal contrast (interaction.ps.hlsl:112-121), which scales the decoded normal's xy by 0.8-1.2 with the per-pixel view vector's z, and _flat does not decode to exactly (0, 0) (about (0.0020, 0.0033): DXT5 alpha 128 and green 128 1/3), so the tilt of the normal, and with it the Lambert term, follows the interpolated view vector. Round 2's R19-R21 (R01-R03's lights on legacy diffuse with bumpmap _flat) differ by 1 on 1,677, 355 and 957 unmasked pixels, mostly on the large floor and ceiling triangles; R14 is exact because its parallel light meets the wall head-on (L near N), where the Lambert term does not feel so small a tilt, not because the wall is uniform. Near-plane clipping only amplifies the effect (a vertex beside or behind the camera carries a view vector almost perpendicular to the view); the parity rows' room split 100 units ahead of the camera (parity.py room_split) stays, harmless. The parity method: R05, R18 and R19-R21 are K28 rows with recorded thresholds (max, mean, p99, the count beyond 1; the mean pins a row's |d| = 1 count), R14 the exact row, the other axial rows +-1 (K28's empirical bound there), R05b reported; the classes live in parity.py's row table. LP7.4 restates it (K44, C55, M-GEO-DIFF-04): the preview draws the .proc's own triangles where its planar islands match the editor's faces (every planar island of the sandbox's four parity .procs and of the fixture's), so the view vector is interpolated over dmap's triangles there and this difference is gone where every face in view is adopted: the 22 k28 rows (R05, R18-R21, A01-A06, G01-G05, M01-M05, B01), the 8 isolated ambient-only shots (K33: A01a, A02a, A06a, G01a-G05a) and the rotated R11 compare max 0 and are exact from LP7.4 on, R05b's envelope is 0, and every axial row but R06 (8 pixels at 1) went from max 1 to 0. K28 is kept for edited faces (an edit on a candidate face returns its island to the editor's triangulation until the next dmap), for unmatched islands and for curved ones (a patch, R10, which stays the patch row; faces within 2.6 degrees that MatchVert welds). Also seen on the fix round's run: dmap snaps brush vertices to its 1/32 grid and removes the faces that lie in slabs thinner than 0.1 between near-coplanar planes (a wall behind panels 0.05 in front of it), and an entity inside such a slab is linked to no area; the preview builds the editor's brushes as they are, so faces closer than 0.1 to another brush's parallel plane can differ in the same way (R13 is built without such faces since round 2).

entries.note: LP4.2b (C38, D91, D95, P4.1, P4.24), test only: the parity run's bake is the engine's own, in an engine process of its own before the shot processes, because LoadSHProbesFile caches the SH list per map name and process (a reload after the bake would keep the empty list of the first load). The bake process (bake.cfg, at most 32 '+' commands, fs_game, fs_savepath and fs_basepath on the command line, FS_GAME asserted before any launch: RemoveFile and OpenFileWrite act under <fs_basepath>/<gameFolder>, the sandbox's tb_parity, never the game/base junction) dmaps and loads the ambient map, waits 120 frames so that the first RenderScene sets tr.primaryWorld and tr.primaryView, sets r_skipInteractions 0 and r_skipAmbient 0 (the captures render full lit views with their shader passes: RDF_NOAMBIENT skips the ambient pass alone) and ui_showGun 0, runs bakeEnvironmentProbes and quits. parity.py checks the .shprobes' entries against the automatic probes of the .proc's areas (PopulateEnvironmentProbes, M-PROBE-01) and every probe's _amb .exr and _amb #__2105, _spec #__2108 and _depth #__2208 caches; the shot processes keep every output of the bake, load the ambient map fresh without a dmap, and their log's LoadSHProbesFile line must report the bake's count. The ambient-only shots: r_skipInteractions 1 (DrawInteractions' only use) around them, printed and checked, and the preview's skipInteractionsForTesting through the row's ambient_only flag (ParityRowSwitch), the frame taken only when its interactions were skipped. The preview root gets the .shprobes, every .bimage, the env_probe entityDef copied out of the game folder and the IBL blobs, never an .exr. A room no entity's origin is in is filled as outside by dmap's flood (the A07 room's func_static block); a translucent material does not seal a room (A07's shell is opaque and unlit, its translucent panel inside). Never in the product; LP4.3 (D91, D95, P4.3, P4.24): the bake process also runs bakeLightGrids -grid ( 128 128 256 ) in a block of its own after the probes: its log's size and per-area shapes are held to SetupLightGrid's of the .proc's area bounds (the probe rooms, z 32..224, have none and no atlas file; the grid rooms, z 0..192 and 0..448, have points and an atlas each); each shot process deletes the .blightgrid by name before its launch and writes its own from the .lightgrid; the preview root takes the .lightgrid with its time and the last shot process's .blightgrid (A2)

entries.note: 39-PATCH-NORMAL-FLAKE.md (F1): a patchDef3's normals are made from uninitialised memory. SubdivideExplicit allocates its vertices with new idDrawVert[] (idDrawVert has no constructor: the block's earlier contents stay), and SampleSinglePatchPoint writes the normal one component at a time, tempNormal = out->GetNormal(), tempNormal[axis - 3] = ..., out->SetNormal( tempNormal ): GetNormal decodes and normalises the bytes already there, so each pass moves the components written before it, and the vertex normal is a function of the heap block's old bytes (up to 62 of 255 a component away from the intended normal, by the investigator's simulation). The GPL Doom 3 original wrote the float components directly (the line commented out after them); the BFG port to byte normals made the dependence. patchDef2 (Subdivide) never reaches it. The engine at 285ea4d1 has it: every dmap of a patchDef3 bakes heap residue into the .proc and .bproc normals, so the fixture's lp1b_geometry.bproc patchDef3 normals are one sample of dmap's heap on the day it was baked. The copy is kept verbatim (C7); the preview subdivides a patchDef3 through the shim's transcription (M-GEO-FN-17), which gathers the three components and calls SetNormal once: the GPL-correct normal, the same on every run and in both builds. An engine defect for the user to file (engine-fixes-plan.md); golden (e) pins the preview's patchDef3 bytes against that one engine sample

39-PATCH-NORMAL-FLAKE.md (F1), the loadSixFileCube precedent (M-IMG-DEFECT-03): the three functions transcribed as members of GatheredPatch, an idSurface_Patch subclass (the protected width, height, maxWidth, maxHeight, expanded and verts), with the private GenerateNormals, GenerateIndexes, Expand, RemoveLinearColumnsRows and Collapse reached through member pointers an explicit instantiation hands out, so the copied class and file stay as they are. engineSubdividePatch makes its patch a GatheredPatch: SetSize, the control points and Subdivide (patchDef2) are the copy's, SubdivideExplicit (patchDef3) the transcription's. The same arithmetic in the same order, the same idDrawVert writes and the same allocation (the tagged new idDrawVert[] of outWidth * outHeight, uninitialised, freed after the copy into verts); SampleSinglePatch's width parameter is named outWidth (it shadowed the member). The one difference: SampleSinglePatchPoint gathers the normal's three components in a local idVec3 and calls SetNormal once after the axis loop (M-GEO-DEFECT-01). The vertices' tangent, fourth normal byte and colours stay unwritten, as in the engine; ChunkBuilder writes them (M-GEO-DIFF-01). Pool-safe as the copy (C24, M-GEO-POOL-02). Tested: the fixture's patchDef3 subdivided with the heap poisoned three ways gives the same written bytes and chunk vertices

entries.note: LP7.4 (C55, D133, D138, P7.1, P7.11, K44, SC638-SC644): the engine always draws dmap's triangles; the preview takes them where they match the editor's faces and keeps its own triangulation elsewhere. dmap groups a side's triangles by (area, material, plane, mergeGroup, texVec within TEXTURE_VECTOR_EQUAL_EPSILON 0.001 and TEXTURE_OFFSET_EQUAL_EPSILON 0.005; usurface.cpp:36-37, 48-106; the texVec M-GEO-FN-18), optimizes each group (OptimizeIsland drops every interior and colinear vertex, optimize.cpp:1967-2000), snaps every vertex to 1/32 and merges it into a hash vertex within one snap unit (up to 3/64 per axis, tritjunction.cpp:80, 122-151), and welds the surface's vertices (MatchVert: xyz 0.01, st 0.001, normal 0.999, output.cpp:127-177); ParseModel recentres the st per island of triangles sharing a vertex (RenderWorld_load.cpp:224-268). The preview partitions each .proc surface into those islands (a union-find makes the walk's partition); an island is planar when every triangle's normal is within 0.999 of its largest triangle's and every vertex within 1/32 of that plane (a patch is one curved island, faces within 2.6 degrees that MatchVert welds too: never adopted). A planar island's candidates are the face pieces (not patches) of its model (a world piece's area, a brush entity's own model, K17) and material (before any remap) whose plane is its own (0.999, the centroid within epsilon = 3/64 + 0.01), whose texture vectors give its st at its vertices (M-GEO-FN-18), and whose polygon overlaps it by more than a sliver; the test: every island vertex within epsilon times the square root of 3 of the candidates' union in the plane, every candidate vertex within it of the island's triangles, no two candidates overlapping beyond a sliver (an addition to C55's test: so that a face moved within its plane, which leaves a strip bare and overlaps its neighbour, cannot pay for the hole with the overlap), and the summed areas within the candidates' perimeter times epsilon; positions as ParseModel reads back what dmap wrote. An adopted island's vertices are loadProcSurface's (loadProcIsland: the same per-vertex code, so the same bytes), its triangles dmap's in their vertex order, tangents by the material's path over it (R_DeriveTangentsWithoutNormals for most, tr_trisurf.cpp:1184-1325, as FinishSurfaces runs it on the area model, Model.cpp:1255-1288; a vertex belongs to one island, so the island's tangents are the whole surface's), back sides from its material, the caster version its chunk's own; the pieces it replaces build no triangles and keep their other roles (references through the island's chunk, the solid count). The evaluation runs after a batch applies, per (entity, model, material) group whose pieces changed, beside the references (M-REF-01), synchronously on the render thread; the islands are built with the bake's read on the parse thread. Measured: the fixture's 37 planar islands of 39 adopted, its 182 adopted vertices byte-equal to the engine's own finished vertices in its .bproc; the sandbox's four parity pairs every planar island adopted (areas 112, stages 420, parity 304 with its patch curved, ambient 182). The differences: an island whose candidate face was edited, or whose faces no longer match for any other reason (a material, an alignment, an overlap), keeps the editor's triangulation until the next dmap (K44), and so does every curved island; a .bproc's finished surfaces are never adopted (D138, M-PROC-02); an island of more than MaxChunkWeldedVerts vertices is not adopted (a chunk holds an island whole); dress fragments (C54) and inlined models' triangles match no face; LP7.3: the dress surfaces it identifies are counted apart (their planar islands leave unmatched_islands, M-DRESS-02), the inlined copies stay counted unmatched (M-DRESS-06)

entries.note: LPF.1 (C40, D98, D102; P5.4, P5.23): the engine replaces a texture of a running world only through reloadImages (ReloadImages): each changed image is purged at once (PurgeImage lets its texture go) and queued, and LoadDeferredImages loads every queued image whole in the same call, through one command list, before the next frame draws; so no frame binds a stand-in (images the level load references are loaded whole too). The preview writes an image's levels within a frame's upload cap (32 MB, low mips first) behind the chunks, and makes no texture within the allocation headroom, so a slot asked again for a changed image (an override, a clear, a re-probed file) while it holds a complete texture is Replacing: the complete texture stays bound with the slot's version (its binding sets stay valid) while the new image is answered, made and written as a Loading slot's, and the frame that writes the new texture's last level swaps it in (its version bumped, the slot's binding sets erased, the old texture retired until the frames in flight have finished, D35; the new image's usage and format become the draws'). A third image before the second landed lets the unfinished texture go and starts again; a headroom refusal (M-ALLOC-DIFF-01) keeps the old texture bound and the image, counted once, the frame unconverged (the livelock guard then waits for another trigger); a format refusal binds the complete texture again (Default). A slot with no complete texture, and an eviction's or a test's drop (dropTexture), go Pending and bind the intrinsic as before (M-IMG-DIFF-11). In-place writeTexture into a non-permanent texture stays deferred (D102). entries.note: LP5.0 step 2 (C49, D69's deferral, P6.20): _fog, 128 x 128 white with the table in alpha: a step table of 0.982 per step (float) over d = idMath::Sqrt of the int sum of squares (x * sqrtf( 1 / x ), the copy's, through engineMathSqrt on the parse thread: intrinsicImage) divided by 63, b = ( byte )( d * 255 ) clamped, then ( byte )( 255 * ( 1.0 - step[b] ) ) (double), 255 on the border; TF_LINEAR (one level), TR_CLAMP, TD_LOOKUP_TABLE_ALPHA, which DeriveOpts stores as FMT_ALPHA: the recipe path now accepts it, and the stored level is the alpha bytes alone (R8_UNORM sampled as (1, 1, 1, R), M-TABLE-07). A function mirror, not a copied range: the range calls idImage::GenerateImage with an nvrhi command list, which the recipe path replaces. The cast of a float past 255 is undefined in C++; it is transcribed as MSVC's x64 code makes it (cvttss2si to a 32-bit int, the low byte kept, msvcByte): 3,803 texels toward the corners take it, d * 255 at (1, 1) is 360.6, cast to 104 (not 255), and the alpha there is 216 where a clamp would give 252; (0, 0) is 110 before the border's 255. The fog shader samples _fog at T = 0.5 (between rows 63 and 64, the planes p1 and p3 of C49), where d stays below 256 / 255, so those texels are never sampled: the engine's behaviour is mirrored (D20), not fixed. The test holds every texel to a transcription written in the test and the sampled rows texel by texel

Derived before the run from the two facts the brief names, the prepass's polygon offset (RenderBackend.cpp:751-755) and the interaction pass without one (:1703), the picture was none: an opaque fragment's depth pulled in front of the wall, so that the depth-equal test passes no pixel of it nor of the wall. entries.note: D147, P3.3 (LP3.1 steps 1 and 3): the engine clears the whole 8192^2 atlas to 1.0 every frame (256 MB of writes); the preview clears each tile it draws by a far-plane quad under the tile's viewport and scissor (builtin/depth, the identity MVP, (+-1, +-1, 1) with w 1, GLS_DEPTHFUNC_ALWAYS | GLS_CULL_TWOSIDED, depth written, no polygon offset: exactly 1.0), and first, by the same quad, every rect last run's tiles occupied that this run's tiles do not cover (tiles_cleared, vacated); NVRHI has no rect clear. Every texel a frame's consumer can sample through a placed side is then the engine's: its tile is cleared and drawn, the rest of the atlas is 1.0 (cleared at creation, M-SHADOW-DIFF-05, or vacated); a vacated rect is cleared on the next frame that runs pass 6 (a frame with no casting light keeps it until then, and no placed side samples it). The [litgpu2] case reads the atlas back: a translucent caster's tiles all 1.0 and a light that left the view leaves its six rects 1.0 LP3.3 (M-SHADOW-DIFF-09, -10): a tile drawn again is cleared first as before, a cached or relocated one is not; the vacated clear covers the parts of last run's rects that no tile of this run covers (uncoveredRects: never a part of a cached or moved tile) and comes after the moves; a clear skipped for a pending pipeline leaves its tile to be drawn again and its vacated rect to be cleared again; case (l) reads a cascade beside a vacated point tile back unchanged and the vacated texels 1.0.

entries.note: LP3.4 step 4 (D158, R5.15, D7), no engine counterpart: the engine at 285ea4d1 declares r_showShadowMaps and BUILTIN_DEBUG_SHADOWMAP but draws neither. The preview's debug views, chosen in the Lit panel (none by default, never by [.][parity] or [.][measure]), draw into ldrFBO after the tonemap pass and before the blit. ShadowAtlas: the 8192² atlas fitted to the view's largest centred square by debug_shadowmap's contract (D147's clip-space quad, the identity MVP, texcoords 0..1 by TEXGEN_0 from its positions with the atlas's first row at the top, level 0, the atlas at set 1 t0, the linear clamp at set 2 s0): each texel's depth in red. It is drawn with the engine's builtin/texture (14, BINDING_LAYOUT_TEXTURE: the same vertex shader, tex.Sample( samp0 ) times rpColor 1), because debug_shadowmap itself cannot draw on Vulkan: its vertex shader writes the clip position to POSITION, not SV_Position, so the SPIR-V has no gl_Position and a vec4 output at location 0 where the fragment shader reads a vec2 (validation VUID-RuntimeSpirv-maintenance4-06817 at the pipeline's creation; nothing rasterized) - an engine defect for the user (E-LIT-15), seen in LP3.4's first run of case (o). TileAge: that picture and every kept tile's rect through builtin/color (1) at alpha 0.5: provisional magenta, relocated this frame blue, drawn this frame green, cached from yellow (age 1) to red (age 64 and more) by log2( age ) / 6. Case (o) checks both pixel by pixel against the atlas's read-back; the PNGs of H01 and H11 are the director's
